question_text: A large tower is to be supported by a series of steel wires; it is estimated that the load on each wire will be $13,300 \mathrm{~N}(3000 \mathrm{lb})$. Determine the minimum required wire diameter, assuming a factor of safety of 2.0 and a yield strength of $860 \mathrm{MPa}(125,000 \mathrm{psi})$ for the steel.The unit of the answer is mm.
response:
The allowable (working) stress is the yield strength divided by the factor of safety:

$$\sigma_w = \frac{860\ \text{MPa}}{2.0} = 430\ \text{MPa}$$

The required cross‑sectional area supports the load at this stress:

$$A = \frac{F}{\sigma_w} = \frac{13{,}300\ \text{N}}{430\times10^{6}\ \text{N/m}^2} \approx 3.093\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2$$

For a circular wire, $A = \pi d^2/4$, so

$$d = \sqrt{\frac{4A}{\pi}} \approx 6.28\ \text{mm}$$

$$\boxed{6.28}$$
